concepts.title: Equal-Area Division of a Square
concepts.definition: A square can be split into 4 equal-area parts in endlessly many ways: start from the obvious four quarters and slide each dividing line so that what one part loses along one edge it gains along another; equal push and pull keeps every part at a quarter of the whole.
concepts.key_idea: Compression on one edge balanced by expansion on another preserves equal areas.

concepts.title: Area of a Rectangle by Unit Squares
concepts.definition: The area of a rectangle counts the unit squares that pack inside it; a grid of so-many rows of so-many columns turns the count into a multiplication, so a rectangle of 5 cm by 3 cm holds 15 unit squares of 1 sq cm.
concepts.key_idea: Rows times columns of unit squares is the whole idea of area.
concepts.textbook_ref: hegp207.txt lines 30-120 (rangoli rectangles, unit square counting)

solution_steps.explain: Length times breadth equals the number of unit squares inside.

concepts.title: Area of a Triangle
concepts.definition: A triangle sits inside a rectangle on the same base and between the same parallels, and it fills exactly half that rectangle, so its area is half the product of base and height.
concepts.key_idea: Drop the altitude, wrap the triangle in its rectangle, then take half.

concepts.title: Area of a Parallelogram
concepts.definition: A parallelogram has the same base-height area relation as a rectangle of equal base and height, because shifting the slanted sides by triangles keeps the region; its area is the base times the perpendicular height, not the slant length.
concepts.key_idea: Cut a triangle off one end and paste it on the other: the slanted box straightens into a rectangle.

concepts.title: Finding a Missing Side from the Area
concepts.definition: Knowing the area of a rectangle, triangle or parallelogram and one dimension recovers the other by undoing the area formula: divide the area by the known base to get the height, as when the height QN of a parallelogram of area 91.2 sq cm on a 7 cm base is sought.
concepts.key_idea: Undo the multiplication: area divided by base leaves the height.
concepts.textbook_ref: hegp207.txt lines 720-740 (Figure it Out Q3 find QN)

concepts.title: Unit Conversions of Length and Area
concepts.definition: Lengths convert linearly - 1 inch is 2.54 cm - but areas convert by the square of the length factor, so 1 square inch is 2.54 x 2.54 = 6.4516 square centimetres, and a 12.7 cm by 12.7 cm square of 161.29 sq cm equals 25 sq in.
concepts.key_idea: Square the length factor for areas: (2.54) squared gives 6.4516 sq cm per sq in.
concepts.textbook_ref: hegp207.txt lines 1140-1160 (2.54 cm, 161.29 sq cm = 6.4516 sq in conversion work)
